style: Say with bright, encouraging energy, like a friendly superhero coach
lines: Welcome, Data Defenders. Three rooms guard Cedar Hollow's data. Tap a door to go in. Solve every puzzle in a room to secure it.
Right now, everyone at Cedar Hollow can open every folder. Lock it down so each person sees only what their job needs, then protect the records account.
Someone changed a grade overnight. Find the changed card, then find out how it happened.
On report card night the school website went down, the server's disk broke, and then the Wi-Fi stopped working. Keep the site up, the work safe and the network running.
Tap a box to take a folder away. Then press Check lock.
Press Use this one on the strongest password. The meter checks your pick.
Add up each card and compare it with its seal. Tap This one was changed on the card that doesn't match.
Tap the row in the log that doesn't fit.
Now pick the first fix.
Change the number of servers, then press Set servers.
Pick the plan that loses the least work.
Sort each part: wired or wireless. Then press Check sort.
The Wi-Fi access point broke. Tap each device that stays online. Then press Check.
Sort every part first. Some parts are not sorted yet.
Tap a card, then tap C, I or A. Then press Open the exit.
Not yet. Look again, or press Clue.
Lock symbol found!
Room C is secured. Confidentiality means only the right people can see the data.
Room I is secured. Integrity means data stays correct, and changes can be checked.
Room A is secured. Availability means data and systems are there when people need them.
Tap Back to hallway and pick another door.
All three rooms are secured. Tap the Exit door to open it.
You escaped! Confidentiality, integrity and availability: Cedar Hollow's data is safe.
Time! Keep going to finish.
Too short, and it uses the school's name.
It uses the school's name, so it is easy to guess.
It is on the common passwords list.
Too short.
Add that card up. Does it match its seal?
That works, but one server would sit idle. Try fewer.
The copy was on the same server, so it broke too. All the work is lost.
The copy is safe in another building, but it is from last Friday. Monday to Thursday are lost.
The copy is in another building, and it was made last night. Only Thursday is lost.
With no copy at all, all the work is lost.
The log is how you found the change. Deleting it hides what happened.
Then anyone could change a grade in secret.
Tap a door to go in. Secure all three rooms to open the exit.
The exit opens when all three rooms are secured. Tap a room door first.
This puzzle is done. Tap another puzzle, or Back to hallway.
This room is secured. Tap Back to hallway and pick another door.
Put all six cards in a slot first. Then press Open the exit.
Keep going to finish.
You escaped! Press Play again to start a new game.
Read each job card. Give a folder only if the job needs it.
Some people need only the public folder.
Longer is stronger.
Stay away from names and common passwords.
Add each card's four scores.
One card adds up to 79.
Look at the times and the devices.
Which change came at night, from a laptop the school does not know?
Find the busiest hour.
Each server handles 500. How many cover 1,400?
A backup on the same machine breaks with it.
More often means less lost.
A cable is wired. A signal through the air is wireless.
When the access point breaks, only the devices on Wi-Fi lose their link.
Ask what went wrong: someone saw it, it was changed, or people could not get to it.
Seen by the wrong people is C. Changed is I. Not there when needed is A.
